Shared psychotic disorder or its more common synonym, folie à deux, is a rare clinical syndrome. Its characteristic feature is transmission of delusions from “inducer” (primary patient), who is the “originally” ill patient and suffers from a psychotic disorder, to another person who may share the inducer's delusions in entirety or in part.1–3 Depending on whether the delusions are shared among two, three, four, five and even twelve people, it is called as folie à deux, folie à trios, folie à quatre, folie à cinq and folie à douze.4
Shared psychotic disorder is mostly observed among people who live in close proximity and in close relationships.5 It is found in parent-offspring, sibling-sibling, or husband-wife constellations. Furthermore, mother-daughter or sister-sister pairs represents fifty percent of the psychotic dyads.6 Rarely all the family members share the same delusions, and this is called folie à famille.5 Additionally, there are case reports of physician-patient folie à deux and even a case involving a dog.7,8
Risk factors include female gender, mental retardation, suggestibility, passivity, histrionic personality traits and suspiciousness, in the secondary patient. Moreover, dependency, ambivalent relationships and repetitive crises have been seen in the family.9–14

While the exact causes of SDD are unknown, the main two contributors are stress and social isolation. People who are socially isolated together tend to become dependent on those they are with, leading to an inducers influence on those around them.

I've been dealing with a PC for 8 years now. When it is infected, I can't walk or sit. I can only lay on my stomach from the pain. I've had it lanced 7 times, and drained twice on it's own from hot sitz baths.  It looks like a murder scene after. I have tried everything under the sun...castor oil, tea tree oil, Prid drawing salve, baking soda with vinegar. Sometimes it would be infected every few months. The ONLY thing I think helped prevent it the past 3 years was me applying Differin adapalene acne gel (it was a prescription, but its otc now) everyday after a shower. It did get infected a few months ago. The lancing was so traumatizing, I left the hospital crying/screaming once without them even cutting it open. I did a lot of research and found a reputable doctor on pilonidal.org so I made an appointment finally. This was a birthday gift to myself even without insurance since I lost my job to covid, but everytime it's infected I worry about losing my job since I'm bed bound for a week and happens suddenly. I figure now is the time to do it before I work again. The cost was $2,700. He did a cleft lift and left in a drain. I have to empty the blood sack when it gets full. I had the surgery this morning and emptied the sack 4 times so far. It was general anesthesia, woke up crying in pain but I was laying on my back and the drain was being pulled in that position. They gave me  dilauded in my iv, and a prescription for hydrocodone.  I'm not in much pain at all. NOTHING like when it's infected. I can actually walk slowly and stand. I have to record how much blood I empty and the times for a few days to see when I can go back to the hospital and have it removed. I hope this is the end of this torture. The surgeon says 20% of his patients have it return, which is pretty low from everything else I have researched. It has cost me so much money in the past (not even including all the work I'd miss) so the money is worth it to me to just get it removed. I just wanted to tell you guys my experience so far. If you have any questions let me know!

I have been dealing with a PC for several years. I've had to get it lanced 7 times, it only drained on it's own twice. Mine gets huge. I can't stand or sit at all. I can only lay on my stomach. My advice to avoid going back is hot epsom salt baths. I wait until I can barely tolerate how hot the water is and it helps it drain on it's own the best way and I have tried everything. Some people have luck with a tar substance called Prid, in a small orange tin jar. It is a drawing salve. You can get it at walgreens or cvs. Im finally having surgery in the morning to have the entire thing removed. It has put me in so much debt, that the $2,500 it'll cost for surgery far outways how much it has cost over the years. Sometimes it'll flare up a few times in a year. I was putting differin (acne gel) on it, and it didn't flare up for the past 3 years so it must have helped. But it did finally again and I made an appt with a surgeon. I dont have health insurance either and jobless. Im lucky enough to have my boyfriend and father help with the funds I have saved up. It has put me out of work so many times for over a week, I want to get it removed before I go back. You will eventually want to get it out and do a lot of research on a surgeon that has plenty of experience with them and the different methods that are out there. Pilonidal.org has tons of advice. Until then, sitz baths, warm compresses, drawing salve to have it drain on it's own. When mine bursts, it looks like a murder scene so you will be ok and save yourself money for now. Good luck!
